text:
sasha: Heads up — I'm seeing repeated Xid 62 and ECC corrected spikes on a couple of eu-west-2 GPU nodes (gpu-12, gpu-17). Need a faster way to pull dmesg/journalctl + nvidia-smi snapshots when this hits so we can decide drain/replace. :eyes:

mike: can you paste a short sample? are errors correlated with high mem?

sasha: from gpu-12 (last 2 boots):
```
[   12.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 62, PID=2432, GPU=0, ChannelID=00000044, HostEngine=eng%
[   12.346000] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
May 12 08:13:20 gpu-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 62
```

infra-bot: automated alert: 3 Xid 62 events in 10m on gpu-12, severity=medium. Logged to infra-telemetry (trace_id=trc_9f3a).

lucy: we should capture these things on the agent side: `dmesg -T --level=err,warn` tail last N lines, `journalctl -k -b --no-pager -n 200`, and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.total,memory.used,ecc.errors.uncorrected,ecc.errors.corrected --format=csv` at the event time. Small example script I use: 
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
OUT=/tmp/gpu-triage-${HOSTNAME}-$(date +%s).tgz
mkdir -p /tmp/gputriage && 
journalctl -k -b --no-pager -n 500 > /tmp/gputriage/journalctl-k.log 2>&1
dmesg -T -n 8 | tail -n 200 > /tmp/gputriage/dmesg.log
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.total,memory.used,ecc.errors.uncorrected,ecc.errors.corrected --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gputriage/nvidia-smi.csv --loop=3 & sleep 4; pkill -f "nvidia-smi --query-gpu"
tar czf $OUT -C /tmp gputriage
echo $OUT
```

teja: +1 on capturing ECC counters. Also correlate with `boot_id` and `dmesg` timestamps so we can tell if error came shortly after resume or during long-run memory pressure. Store with labels: node, gpu_index, boot_id, trace_id.

mike: what about retention and noise? we don't want logs exploding. proposal: only collect full bundle on Xid >= 62 (or repeated Xid/uncorrected ecc), otherwise send a single-line alert with `nvidia-smi --query` snapshot and `journalctl -k -n 50`. keep bundle TTL 7d, and just metrics for 90d.

sasha: makes sense. For now I'll add a tiny job in the node-agent: on Xid or uncorrected ecc event -> create triage bundle via script above and upload to s3://redwood-gpu-triage/eu-west-2/<node>/<ts>.gz, tag with trace_id. I'll also add a short message to slack channel with the S3 link and the minimal snapshot so oncall can decide drain/replace quickly. :shipit:

lucy: one more thing — include `/proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/information` and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,ERRORS` in the bundle. sometimes ECC corrected counts accumulate and tell different story.

mike: nice. can infra-bot add a quick summary feature? e.g., on upload post summary: node, gpu, Xid_count, uncorrected_ecc, s3_link.

infra-bot: noted. will add a follow-up PR for summary formatting and retention policy.

sasha: thanks team — I'll push a small change to the agent and ping here when deployed.

teja: if you want a sample parser for quick triage, I have a tiny awk/python that extracts the last Xid lines + ECC deltas — I can drop it in the PR.

sasha: please do. that will speed manual triage a lot.
